## How `@someone` becomes a notification

**1. Parsing the handle out of the comment text.**
When a comment is saved, `src/server/services/comment-service.ts`'s `createComment(actor, input)` calls `resolveMentionedUsers(orgId, input.body, input.mentionedUserIds)`. That function loads the org's member roster (`memberRepo.listMembers({ orgId, limit: 100, cursor: null })`) and hands the body plus that member list to `src/lib/mentions.ts`. There, `extractMentions(body)` strips fenced/inline code (`withoutCode`) and runs `MENTION_PATTERN = /(^|[\s(<[])@([a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,38}[a-z0-9])/gi` via `matchAll`, returning distinct lowercased handles in order of first appearance.

**2. Turning the handle into a real user.**
`handleOf(member)` in the same file defines a member's handle as the local part of their email (`email.split("@")[0]`, lowercased). `resolveMentions(body, members)` builds a `handle -> UserId` map from the org members, looks up each extracted handle in it, and silently drops anything that doesn't match a known member (typos just vanish, no error). `resolveMentionedUsers` in `comment-service.ts` unions this server-resolved set with any client-supplied `input.mentionedUserIds` (filtered to only actual org members) — the server-derived list wins on any disagreement.

**3. What carries the list forward.**
The result is a plain `readonly UserId[]` called `mentionedUserIds`. `createComment` writes it onto the comment row via `commentRepo.insertComment({ ...input, mentionedUserIds }, actor.userId)`, and — more importantly for notifications — attaches the same array to the domain event it emits: `emit("comment.created", { ...actorEnvelope(actor), commentId, issueId, mentionedUserIds })` (`src/lib/event-bus.ts`). Downstream code reads this field straight off the event rather than re-parsing the markdown.

**4. Fan-out and persistence.**
`src/server/services/notification-service.ts` subscribes to `"comment.created"` (wired up at boot through `event-registry.ts` / `instrumentation.ts`). Its handler first notifies watchers, then, if `mentionedUserIds` is non-empty, calls `notify(orgId, "comment_mention", mentionedUserIds, { title, body, href, actorId })`. `notify()` dedupes recipients, skips the comment's own author, and for each remaining recipient loads their preference row via `preferenceRepo.getPreference(orgId, recipientId, "comment_mention")` (`src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts`).

**5. In-app vs. email vs. nothing.**
`resolveChannels(preference, flags)` in `notification-service.ts` makes the call: if the user has no preference row yet, they get the default `["in_app", "email"]`; otherwise `in_app` is included only if `preference.inApp`, and `email` only if `preference.email` and either they aren't `digestOnly` or the org's `digest_email` feature flag is off. If the resulting channel list is empty, that recipient gets no notification row at all. Whoever remains gets a row batch-inserted by `notificationRepo.insertNotifications(orgId, rows)` (`src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts`) into the `notifications` table, with the chosen `channels` array stored as JSON on the row.

**6. The email that (almost) happens.**
There's a real `MentionEmail` template (`src/emails/mention-email.tsx`) wired into `src/emails/render.ts` and known to `email-service.ts` as the `"mention"` `EmailTemplate`, but nothing in the codebase actually calls `renderEmail("mention", ...)` / `sendEmail(...)` for it. The `channels` field on the notification row is written but never read to trigger an immediate send — it looks like scaffolding that was never connected. The only email a mention can actually produce is via the daily digest path: `digestOnly` recipients' unread mention notifications get swept up by `runDigestEmailJob` (`src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts`, driven by `src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts`), which calls into `src/server/services/digest-service.ts` (`listDigestRecipients`, `buildDigest`) and ultimately `sendEmail("digest", ...)`.

So: a normal (non-digest) recipient with mentions enabled ends up with just an in-app row despite the row saying `channels: ["in_app","email"]`; a `digestOnly` recipient with the `digest_email` flag on eventually gets one batched email the next time the digest job runs; anyone with mention notifications turned off in preferences gets nothing at all.
